label: GTR GRID/DIA authority graph
description: Authority graph showing how GTR governance, national registrar authority, GRID publication, DIA issuance, and relying-party verification are bounded by scope and revocation semantics.

nodes.label: GRID governance authority
nodes.scope: Defines participation, eligibility, technical standards, and suspension pathways
nodes.authorityOrigin: GTR governance charter or administering-body mandate

nodes.label: Member State or competent national authority
nodes.scope: Recognizes or identifies the registrar responsible for a domestic register
nodes.authorityOrigin: national law, regulation, official designation, or equivalent legal instrument

nodes.label: Authoritative Registrar
nodes.scope: Maintain the named register, publish GRID metadata, and issue DIA within declared register scope
nodes.authorityOrigin: delegated or recognized by national authority

nodes.label: Global Registrar Information Directory
nodes.scope: Publish registrar discovery metadata, verification material, lifecycle state, and release history

nodes.label: GRID technical operator and harvester
nodes.scope: Validate, harvest, publish, monitor, and archive GRID records under operating rules

nodes.label: Digital Identity Anchor
nodes.scope: Credential artifact issued by the registrar to a registered entity
nodes.authorityOrigin: issued within registrar mandate and DIA issuance policy

nodes.label: GRID eligibility and reliance policy
nodes.scope: Constrains admission, metadata, keys, lifecycle status, and relying-party acceptance

nodes.label: Verifier and relying party
nodes.scope: Verify DIA and GRID evidence before admitting an operational effect

edges.scopeConstraint: policy covers GRID admission, publication, suspension, and release behavior
edges.revocationSemantics: policy supersession changes future admission and relying decisions
loss of national mandate requires registrar suspension or revocation in GRID

edges.scopeConstraint: must provide authority evidence, metadata, contact, lifecycle state, and verification material where applicable
edges.revocationSemantics: eligibility failure can suspend or revoke GRID participation

edges.scopeConstraint: publication limited to approved registrar metadata and release artifacts
edges.revocationSemantics: compromised metadata must be removed, superseded, or flagged before new reliance

edges.scopeConstraint: metadata, keys, endpoints, status, and supported capabilities only
edges.revocationSemantics: stale or withdrawn metadata must not admit high-impact new effects

edges.scopeConstraint: DIA claims must be covered by registrar mandate and register scope
edges.revocationSemantics: issuer suspension changes future DIA verification outcomes

edges.scopeConstraint: verifier checks issuer discoverability, lifecycle state, scope, key, freshness, and revocation
edges.revocationSemantics: revoked or unavailable status blocks, downgrades, or routes reliance to review

delegationChains.terminationCondition: withdrawal of legal mandate, expiry, suspension, or GRID eligibility failure
operator mandate revoked, release process suspended, or integrity incident

revocationRules.trigger: Registrar legal authority is withdrawn or superseded
revocationRules.effect: Registrar GRID status changes to revoked and new DIA reliance is blocked or routed to review

revocationRules.trigger: Registrar signing key or metadata publication key is compromised
revocationRules.effect: Affected key is suspended, GRID record is updated, and new verification must reject or review affected DIAs

revocationRules.trigger: GRID record exceeds freshness policy or required status source becomes unavailable
revocationRules.effect: High-impact reliance is downgraded, warned, or routed to manual review

notes: Authority is not inferred from self-description. It is evidenced and scoped.
GRID publication improves discovery but does not replace domestic legal authority.
The verifier is responsible for converting evidence into a relying-party effect under policy.
